learningObjective: Reason about the trade-offs of calling external libraries (cuBLAS, cuDNN, cutlass, MKL) from a compiled runtime versus emitting compiler-generated kernels.

canonicalClaims.claim: External vendor libraries usually outperform compiler-generated kernels on standard GEMM/Conv patterns due to hand-tuned per-architecture code; compilers earn back an advantage by fusing ops adjacent to those kernels (bias, activation, epilogue) that the library cannot see.
conditions: Standard shapes and dtypes supported by the vendor library.
Compiler has the capability to fuse producer/epilogue ops into a single kernel.
nonImplications: Does not imply compilers always lose in isolation; specialized shapes/dtypes may favor generation.
Does not imply fusion is universally possible.

misconceptions.claim: External libraries replace the runtime allocator.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Libraries request workspace from the runtime; they do not own the allocator.

misconceptions.claim: cuBLAS/cuDNN outputs are bitwise stable across versions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Algorithm selection can change across versions, changing low-order bits.

misconceptions.claim: Compiler-generated kernels are always faster than vendor libs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Generation wins primarily via fusion; isolated GEMM/Conv usually favors the vendor lib.

misconceptions.claim: Calling external libs is free of ABI risk.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Library ABI upgrades can break loading or change semantics; version pinning matters.
